summary: I tested the corner (eps > 1, v* <~ 10-30 km/s, sigma ~ v*) of Paul's hypothetical long-range chi-only gated attraction in two ways: a global N-body toy, and small-scale-structure proxies with live-searched data. Setup: direct-summation runs of a cored (Plummer) chi halo; N = 2000; three realizations per case; an eps = 0 control; the gated term switched on adiabatically. The main reading is the record-faithful Hamiltonian one (gate on canonical momentum); the force-law reading was run once for comparison. At eps = 1, 3 and 10, with v* = sigma_0 and 2.5 sigma_0, no velocity-selected structure appeared: no co-moving clumps, streams or coherent flows beyond the control. An injection test puts the sensitivity at about 1-3% of the mass, over 43 central free-fall times after the switch-on. The Hamiltonian reading reorganizes the halo instead. Canonical momenta narrow, so the gate opens further (realized sigma_c/v* = 0.42-0.73). The kinematic dispersion becomes 1.5-11.5 times the canonical one. The halo expands (v* = sigma_0) or contracts (v* = 2.5 sigma_0). The force-law reading contracts and heats it. Both nulls agree with the re-virialized local model at the realized gate ratios. Not tested: slower instabilities, and anything below the two-body relaxation floor (energy diffusion scales as N^-1/2). On observations, linear growth in both readings changes the small-scale power by large factors near k v* ~ 1. Four probes constrain the corner: (1) against WDM-equivalent tolerances from the high-resolution Lyman-alpha bounds, eps = 1 is beyond the 5.3-keV deviation at 0.1 s/km for v* >= 5 km/s in both readings; (2) the Planck optical depth and (3) dwarf central densities exclude eps = 3 at v* = 5-30 km/s and eps = 1 at v* >~ 20-30 km/s; (4) early dense chi clumps would overheat Segue 1 at eps = 1 for v* = 3-20 km/s if they survive, while eps = 0.3 passes. The satellite equivalence-principle test is blind there. Any clumping in the corner would be decorative: nothing in the record fixes eps, no carrier exists, and the corner's gate scale is 4-12 times below the record's v* = 120 km/s. Net: in linear theory and both readings, the corner is excluded for eps >~ 3 and disfavoured for eps ~ 1 at v* >~ 3-5 km/s. What remains open (eps <~ 0.3-1 at v* <~ 3-5 km/s) is where neither the local model nor the N-body gives velocity-selected structure.

claims.statement: Reading and model used. The corner model U = -G~ m^2 W(|w-w'|/v*)/r (W = exp(-s^2/2), eps = G~/G, added to gravity, chi only) was integrated as a Hamiltonian H = sum p^2/2m + sum U(x_ij, p_ij), with the gate on the canonical momentum per mass w = p/m: xdot_i = w_i + (eps G m/v*^2) sum_j W_ij (w_i - w_j)/r_ij (anomalous velocity), wdot_i = -G m sum_j (1 + eps W_ij)(x_i - x_j)/r_ij^3. Why: #11 sec. 8 puts the gate on the incoming relative momentum k, a canonical momentum; the Hamiltonian form conserves energy, momentum, angular momentum and phase-space volume, so round 2's mean-field (Vlasov) picture applies; the force-law reading (xdot = w, force at fixed velocity) follows from no Lagrangian (critic D1) and does not conserve phase-space volume, so it was run only as a comparison (eps = 3). The model itself is a hypothetical outside the record (round 2 C16: X massive, lambda_X < 37.7 um).
claims.basis: Hamilton's equations for the pair energy; the C kernel was verified against a direct numpy evaluation and against finite-difference derivatives of H (Q3).

claims.statement: Negative result: the self-consistent isotropic equilibrium solver f = A(-e)^(7/2), e = w^2/2 + Phi(r) + Phig(r,|w|), did not converge for eps > 0. A first version drifted in scale until the grid truncated the halo, showing up as a virial residual equal to the surface term. A version with the half-mass radius pinned each iteration left residuals of 1e-2 to 4 after 4000 iterations. The eps > 0 halos were therefore built dynamically, by switching the gate on adiabatically inside the N-body (Q3). The eps = 0 anchor reproduces the Plummer sphere.
claims.basis: equilibrium.py: 2D (r, |w|) grid with the angle-averaged Gaussian gate kernel and shell-theorem potentials. Anchors are textbook Plummer formulas [T]: rho = (3/4pi)(1+r^2)^-5/2, sigma_0^2 = 1/6, F = 24 sqrt2/(7 pi^3) (-E)^(7/2).

claims.statement: N-body setup and verification. Direct-summation C kernel (O(N^2), no memory load); implicit-midpoint integrator (symplectic, time-symmetric; dt = 0.01, fixed-point tolerance 1e-9); Plummer softening b = 0.1 on both channels; units G = M = a = 1. Initial conditions: the Plummer sphere. eps(t) = eps_f(3u^2 - 2u^3), u = t/15, then held fixed to t = 40. v* = sigma_0/r_g with sigma_0 = sqrt(1/6) (gravitational velocity scale), r_g = 1 and 0.4. Runs: N = 2000, 3 seeds each, at eps = 0, 1, 3, 10 (H reading), plus eps = 3 in the F reading; N = 1000 at eps = 0 and 10 to test N-dependence; 29 runs in all. After the ramp, energy is conserved to <= 1.8e-5 (H), momentum to ~1e-17, and angular momentum to all printed digits. The F reading drifts in energy by 2-4%, as expected for a non-conservative force law. Two-body relaxation time for gravity alone (Spitzer form [T, dagger]): 61.5 units at N = 2000.

claims.statement: Main global-dynamics result: no velocity-selected structure appears in a cored, self-gravitating chi halo with sigma ~ v* at eps = 1, 3 or 10, in either reading. Over t = 20-40 (3 seeds), all differences from the eps = 0 control are small: the 6D pair excess Xi(v*/2) (pairs closer than 0.25 r50 in position and v*/2 in canonical momentum, relative to shell-reassigned velocities) differs by +0.014 to +0.039, each within 2 standard errors; Xi(v*) by +0.007 to +0.023; stream statistics S1 and S2 by <= 0.16 (S1 is at most 3.9 sigma, because the control sits below its isotropic value of 0); bulk-flow power R_v by +0.03 +- 0.03 in the H runs. None of these grows: the slopes of Xi(v*/2) are within the spread of the control's own slopes. The F reading shows a marginal R_v excess (+0.103 +- 0.037) with no counterpart in Xi or S_l. The small positive Xi(v*) offsets do not grow with eps (+0.0137 at eps = 1, +0.0086 at eps = 10, r_g = 1), consistent with two-body correlations of order (1 + eps W)/N rather than a collective mode (interpretation). For comparison, injecting 2% of the particles as co-moving clumps raises Xi(v*/2) by 0.15 in one snapshot, and 5% raises it by 0.46; a 5% stream raises S1 by 0.87 and S2 by 0.93.
claims.basis: diagnostics.py on all 29 runs, aggregated as mean +- standard error over seeds; summary_numbers.py for differences from the control; injection_test.py for sensitivity.

claims.statement: Instead of clumping, the Hamiltonian reading reorganizes the halo. Canonical momenta narrow, so the gate measured on them opens further: realized core sigma_c/v* = 0.73, 0.61, 0.54 at eps = 1, 3, 10 (r_g = 1), and 0.42, 0.45, 0.48 (r_g = 0.4), against 0.90 in the control. Kinematic velocities (xdot) become much larger than canonical ones: sigma_kin/sigma_c = 1.77, 3.88, 11.5 (r_g = 1) and 1.48, 2.40, 5.49 (r_g = 0.4). The halo expands at r_g = 1 (r50 x1.25, x1.48, x1.65) and contracts at r_g = 0.4 (x0.87, x0.80, x0.74). The force-law reading at eps = 3 contracts it (r50 x0.685) and heats it, with realized sigma/v* = 1.25. So whether chi-only extra gravity makes a dwarf halo denser or puffier depends on the reading and the gate width. In the H reading the gate keeps acting on canonical momenta even when physical velocities exceed v* by large factors.

claims.statement: Relaxation and the window. The rms change of each particle's mean-field energy grows as N^-1/2: the ratio N=1000/N=2000 is 1.425 at eps = 0 and 1.369 at eps = 10, against sqrt2 = 1.414. So that evolution is two-body relaxation, not a collective mode. The gate speeds relaxation up: the squared ratio to the control is 6.0 at eps = 10 (H) and 16 for the F reading at eps = 3 (partly from its contraction). The 43-free-fall-time window corresponds to 0.37-0.64 Gyr in a classical dSph core and 0.12 Gyr in Segue 1. A dwarf's 10 Gyr spans 668-1155 such times (3683 in Segue 1). The run therefore excludes velocity-selected instabilities with e-folding times shorter than roughly the window, at the sensitivity of Q4. Slower collisionless instabilities, and anything below the relaxation floor, are not excluded.

claims.statement: The global null agrees with round 2's local model once the equilibrium absorbs the gate's binding (re-virialization) and the realized gate ratio is used. The ratio Lambda_g/<W> caps the effect: below the core margin Q = 1.0966 for r <= 0.66 (1.0228 at r = 0.4, 1.0580 at 0.55, 1.0929 at 0.66), so no eps destabilizes there. At r = 1 the onset is eps = 9.78, at r = 1.5 it is 12.1, and the force-law run's realized r = 1.25 lies between them, above its eps = 3. The l = 1 (velocity-dipole) caps are 0.13-0.47 for r <= 1, so those modes never go unstable. Without re-virialization, the crossover 1/Lambda_g at the realized r (1.5-2.3) is below eps = 3 and 10, yet no velocity-selected mode appeared. The global halo behaves as the re-virialized picture says, well beyond the local model's validity limit (eps < 1.26-2.0 at these r).

claims.statement: High-resolution Lyman-alpha forest (task 2d). In velocity units the gate acts at y = k v* (the same at every z), so k = 0.05-0.2 s/km probes y ~ 1 for v* ~ 5-20 km/s, where the compressed DESI pivot is barely affected. The two readings respond oppositely at those scales. Force-law (K4): enhancement for y >~ 0.5. Hamiltonian (c4b): suppression at y ~ 1-2, then enhancement for y >~ 2.5. The tolerance proxy is the WDM suppression at the published bounds, 5.3 keV (smooth thermal history) and 3.5 keV (non-smooth) [S]: allowed |T^2 - 1| at 0.1 s/km is 0.045 and 0.121 (z = 4.2). Result: eps = 1 exceeds the 5.3-keV deviation at 0.1 s/km for every v* >= 5 km/s in both readings, and the 3.5-keV deviation for v* >= 7 (H; except v* = 20, where H passes near T^2 = 1) and for v* >= 5 (K4). eps >= 3 is beyond both at v* >= 5 km/s, by factors of several to orders of magnitude. At v* = 3 km/s, eps = 1 passes in H and only exceeds the 5.3-keV level in K4. eps = 0.3 passes in H for v* <= 7 km/s but exceeds 3.5 keV in K4 for v* >= 10.

claims.statement: Reliability of the linear theory used in Q8 and Q10-Q13. Both systems' implementations reproduce the analytic uniform-limit Einstein-de Sitter growth exponents to five digits. The Hamiltonian-reading system (critic c4b, unreviewed) leaves its regular regime at eps >= 2.25-2.29: the coefficient (1 + b) of the velocity term then crosses zero near y = 1.42, so its predictions at eps >= 3 are not trustworthy. The force-law (K4) reading gives exclusions there on its own. For eps >= 3, both readings put all scales <~ 1e4-1e6 Msun beyond collapse before z = 150, so linear theory itself breaks down and the proxies are only qualitative there.

claims.statement: Central densities of dwarfs (task 2a). Inside dwarfs with v* > sigma the gated term acts as extra chi-only gravity, and stars measure only the gravitational mass, so the test runs through formation epochs. Proxy: the 1-sigma collapse redshift (sigma(M, z_c) = 1.686), with density scaling as (1+z_c)^3. For 1e9 Msun, typical of classical-dSph pre-infall masses (0.8-22e9 Msun [S]), the density ratio to LCDM is: eps = 1: x0.95/x1.24 (H/K4) at v* = 5, x0.97/x2.17 at 10, x2.14/x6.6 at 20, x5.0/x14.7 at 30 km/s. eps = 3: x38-2000. eps = 10: no collapse epoch, since everything collapses before z = 150. The observed rho_DM(150 pc) = 0.79-2.36e8 Msun/kpc^3 is CDM-consistent per Read et al. [S], so factors >~ 2 would be in tension. That excludes eps = 3 at v* = 5-30 km/s and eps = 1 at v* >~ 20 km/s (H) or >~ 10 km/s (K4), within this proxy.
claims.basis: obs_corner.py part B gives sigma(M,z) from the EH98 LCDM spectrum times the gated T^2 (both readings). The proxy follows dark-tests K11. It assumes the gate stays open through collapse; for halos whose virial velocity exceeds v* the gate partly closes, so it overstates the effect there (inference).

claims.statement: Reionization optical depth (task 2c). Toy model: Q(z) = min(1, zeta f_coll(>1e8 Msun)), with Press-Schechter f_coll from the gated sigma(M,z). Calibrated in LCDM it gives tau = 0.054, completion at z = 5.65 and midpoint z = 7.05. Two calibrations for the gated models: (i) the same zeta; (ii) zeta re-fit so reionization ends at z = 6. Against Planck tau = 0.054 +- 0.007 [S], under (ii): eps = 1 gives 0.057/0.059 (H/K4) at v* = 5, 0.056/0.068 at 10, 0.071/0.101 at 20, 0.097/0.136 at 30 km/s. eps = 3 gives >= 0.188 at every v* = 5-30. So eps = 3 is excluded and eps = 1 is excluded for v* >~ 20 km/s (K4) or >~ 30 km/s (H), unless the ionizing efficiency of early halos is suppressed by large factors. Milky Way satellite counts, as a WDM-template proxy (6.5 keV [S]), bound only the H reading's suppression: eps = 1 at v* = 3-5 km/s is beyond it at k = 10-20/Mpc. The K4 enhancement is not bounded by counts alone. High-z galaxy abundance was not computed.

claims.statement: Ultra-faint-dwarf heating (task 2e). Early, dense chi clumps would heat Segue 1's stars through gravity alone. The heating rate, derived here from Chandrasekhar's coefficients [T] for massless stars in a Maxwellian of clumps, is d sigma_*^2/dt = (8 sqrt(2pi)/3) G^2 f rho M_c lnL sigma_c^2/(sigma_c^2 + sigma_*^2)^(3/2). With Segue 1's sigma = 3.7 km/s, M(<r_1/2) = 5.8e5 Msun and R_1/2 = 29 pc [S] (mean DM density 2.40 Msun/pc^3), over 12 Gyr [dagger] and with lnL = 5, compact clumps must satisfy sum f M_c < 7.88 Msun. Only clumps that collapsed at z > 87.7 are denser than Segue 1 (mapping of Graham & Ramani 2024 [S]). Press-Schechter heating moment at that epoch: LCDM 4e-15 Msun. eps = 0.3: <= 0.002 Msun at v* = 3-20 km/s. eps = 1: 34-39 (v* = 3), 131-164 (5), 742-1050 (10), 2690-5030 (20) Msun. eps = 2: 3e3-2e4 Msun. If the clumps survive and are compact, eps >~ 1 is excluded at v* >= 3 km/s.

claims.statement: Equivalence-principle and tidal tests in satellites (task 2b) are blind in the corner. The gate between a satellite's chi and the host's chi is closed at orbital speeds. For Sgr in a 150 km/s host (round-2 inputs), <W> = 4.3e-6, 3.5e-5, 2.8e-4 and 9.5e-4 at v* = 5, 10, 20 and 30 km/s; a 10% EP limit therefore gives eps < 2.3e4, 2.9e3, 359 and 105. Stars and chi fall alike toward the host. Inside the satellite the gate is open (Segue 1: sigma/v* = 0.74, 0.37, 0.12 at v* = 5, 10, 30), so chi is more tightly self-bound than the gravitational mass the stars trace. That shifts the chi tidal radius outward relative to the stars and would leave stellar stripping unchanged at a given mass profile; no bound was computed.

claims.statement: Other probes (task 2e). The CMB and large-scale structure are blind: the comoving gate radius v*/(aH) is 7.0 kpc at z = 1090 and 148.5 kpc at z = 0 for v* = 10 km/s (20.9 and 445.4 kpc for 30 km/s). Not computed, but expected to bear on the early dense clumps: strong-lensing flux ratios, stellar-stream gaps, cosmic-dawn 21-cm, and dynamical friction in dwarfs. On the last, chi wakes with enhanced self-gravity would raise friction, the opposite of the founding image's suppressed friction (inference).

Mandatory or decorative (task 3): any clumping in the corner would be a free add-on. (i) The record does not fix eps and has no carrier for a long-range gated chi-chi force. X is massive (lambda_X < 37.7 um, round 2 C16) and the massless graviton is ungated. A gravitational-strength 1/r force scatters at about 2.4e-62 cm^2/g at 30 km/s (round 2 K16), so the sigma_0 fit cannot fix eps. (ii) No observation the program must explain requires the corner. Its effects make dwarfs denser (K4/force-law) or suppress power at k v* ~ 1 (H), and neither is a program commitment. (iii) The corner's gate scale is 4-12 times below the record's v* = 120 km/s. At the record's v*, dwarfs have sigma << v*, the term is plain extra chi gravity, and compressed DESI limits it to eps <~ 0.03-0.34 (round 2). The corner therefore needs a second, independent gate scale. (iv) In any case, the N-body found no clumping up to eps = 10 (Q4).

claims.statement: Map in (eps, v*) (task 4), linear-theory proxies in both readings (H/K4), plus N-body. EXCLUDED: eps >~ 3 at v* = 5-30 km/s (tau(ii) >= 0.188 against 0.054 +- 0.007; dwarf densities x15-2000; Lyman-alpha beyond the 3.5-keV deviation; Segue 1 heating >= 3e3 Msun already at eps = 2). eps = 1 at v* = 20-30 km/s (tau(ii) 0.071-0.136; densities x2.1-14.7; Lyman-alpha beyond 5.3 keV (H) or 3.5 keV (K4); Segue 1 heating 2.7e3-5.0e3 Msun). DISFAVOURED (template-level or conditional on clump survival): eps ~ 1 at v* = 3-10 km/s. Here Lyman-alpha is beyond the 5.3- or 3.5-keV deviation at 0.1 s/km in both readings for v* >= 5, and only in K4 at v* = 3; Segue 1 heating is 34-1050 Msun against 7.88. OPEN: eps <~ 0.3-1 at v* <~ 3-5 km/s (H) or <~ 3 km/s (K4). There the gate is open only in the coldest ultra-faints, and the local model plus N-body give no velocity-selected structure. VELOCITY-SELECTED STRUCTURE: none in any case run (eps = 1-10; realized sigma_c/v* = 0.42-0.73 in H and 1.25 in F), within ~43 central free-fall times and ~1-3% of the mass. The round-2 compressed-DESI bounds at v* = 10 (eps < 3.04 K4, 6.80 consistent) are much weaker than these high-k probes.

claims.statement: Literature context. Graham & Ramani 2024 show that stellar heating in ultra-faint dwarfs constrains small-scale power at k ~ 10-1000/Mpc, orders of magnitude beyond earlier bounds. They use Segue 1 with R_* = 24.7 pc and collapsed-fraction clump densities rho_s ~ (Delta/2.317) rho_crit Omega_m (1+z)^3, which Q12 adopts. Costa et al. 2025 ('Dark forces suppress structure growth') find that minimal scalar-mediated dark-matter forces do not enhance growth in CMB-compatible scenarios. Strong-lensing flux ratios, stellar-stream gaps and cosmic-dawn 21-cm as tests of early dense chi clumps; dynamical friction in dwarfs with self-gravitating chi wakes.

Whether the Hamiltonian reading's decoupling of kinematic and canonical velocities (up to 11.5x) is physical or a sign that a classical many-body H with a long-range momentum-gated term is not the right limit of the record's quantum amplitude.
caveats: The model is hypothetical, not in the record. The record's X is massive and its gate acts at contact range.

The N-body is an isolated Plummer halo with the gate switched on adiabatically, not a cosmological formation history. N = 2000 with softening b = 0.1 means two-body relaxation is present, and the gate accelerates it (x6 in squared energy diffusion at eps = 10). Only gate ratios r_g = 0.4 and 1 were run, and the F reading only at eps = 3.
The self-consistent F(e) solver failed for eps > 0, so no exact gated equilibrium was available; the adiabatic switch-on provides a dynamical one.

All observational limits use linear-theory proxies. These are: 1-sigma collapse redshifts with (1+z_c)^3 densities; a Press-Schechter toy reionization with Y_p = 0.245 [dagger]; WDM-template tolerances that are not likelihoods (an enhancement is treated like a suppression); and a Segue 1 heating estimate that assumes clump survival, compactness, lnL = 5, a 12 Gyr age [dagger] and Delta sigma^2 < sigma^2. Where the effects are huge (eps >= 3) the conclusion is robust to these; at eps ~ 1 it is not.
The H-reading linear system (critic c4b) is unreviewed and irregular for eps >= 2.25, so H-reading numbers at eps >= 3 are not trustworthy; the K4 reading gives the exclusions there.
